x:
The Andhra Mahasabha was founded in 1930 at Jogipet (Medak district) with the objective of promoting the social, educational and cultural advancement of Telugu-speaking people in the Hyderabad State. The first session was presided over by Madapati Hanumantha Rao, who is popularly known as the "Andhra Pitamaha." Initially, the organisation concentrated on social reforms, promotion of the Telugu language and expansion of education. Gradually, it developed into an important political platform that opposed the autocratic rule of the Nizam and spread political consciousness among the people of Telangana. During the 1940s, many of its leaders became associated with the peasant movement against feudal oppression. Therefore, the statement that it was established to support the policies of the Nizam Government is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
